title: Your LLM App Returned 200 OK. It Was Still Wrong. — Marina Petzel, Datadog
talk_summary: A Datadog advocate argues that traditional golden signals (latency, errors, traffic, saturation) are insufficient for LLM apps, which need an added layer of cost, safety, and quality monitoring. She catalogs concrete metrics and attribution strategies: token creep, model drift, redundant calls, per-feature/user/model/endpoint cost tagging, PII/jailbreak detection, and hallucination/relevance/completeness scoring.

takeaways.what_they_do: Tag every LLM call by feature/intent, user/org, model/provider, and endpoint/environment so spend can be attributed and benchmarked rather than seen as one undifferentiated blob.
Watch for silent context-window growth and for model swaps to pricier models, both of which blow budgets without usage changing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: engineers or product managers trying to improve the quality quietly increasing the context window ... up to eight x cost increased
takeaways.numbers: context 4k→132k tokens ≈ 8x cost; Opus ~15x per-request cost vs cheaper model

takeaways.what_they_do: Add a caching layer so identical queries don't repeatedly hit the expensive model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 70% of the spend sometimes are redundant because the system is paying for exactly the same expensive model completion
takeaways.numbers: ~70% redundant spend claimed (vendor research, treat skeptically)

takeaways.what_they_do: Score outputs on hallucination rate, relevance, completeness (LLM-judge), and user satisfaction rather than a single 200-OK or binary gate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 200 okay response from your server doesn't necessarily mean that the answer was helpful or correct

takeaways.technique: Output scanning for PII and injection
takeaways.what_they_do: Scan all model outputs for PII (regex/NER) and detect prompt-injection/jailbreak patterns with classifiers, targeting zero leakage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: scan all the model outputs for sensitive data ... only acceptable target should be 0% of your production outputs

takeaways.what_they_do: Because same prompt yields different outputs, run continuous quality evals in the live environment instead of relying on regression tests alone.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we cannot rely on the standard regression testing alone. And you must constantly evaluate quality in the live environment
